note: Defects and traps were planted deliberately. Every one is verifiable from target.md plus repo/.

defects.title: Client-chosen image/* content type (including SVG) is stored and served from the app's own origin without nosniff, CSP or attachment disposition: stored XSS
defects.where: target.md 'Upload flow' step 2 and the paragraph on accepting any image/* type, and 'Serving'; repo/src/avatars/presign.py (only checks startswith('image/')), repo/infra/cdn.yaml (/avatars/* passes origin headers through on app.pixelnest.example and omits the nosniff and CSP headers that only the /* behavior adds)
defects.detect_if: says a user can upload an active-content image type such as image/svg+xml (the check only requires an image/ prefix and the client picks the type), that the original is served as-is with that Content-Type from the same origin as the app (no nosniff / CSP / Content-Disposition on the /avatars/* behavior), so a script in the file runs in the app's origin when opened (stored XSS / session theft). A generic 'validate file types' remark without the same-origin serving consequence does not count
defects.fixed_if: restricts accepted types to an explicit raster allowlist enforced by storage or re-encoding, and/or serves user media from a separate origin or with Content-Disposition: attachment, nosniff and a restrictive CSP

defects.title: Thumbnailer's trigger prefix (avatars/) includes its own output prefix (avatars/thumb/): the function re-triggers itself indefinitely
defects.where: target.md 'Object layout' (thumbs under avatars/thumb/) and 'Thumbnails'; repo/infra/storage.tf (filter_prefix = "avatars/"), repo/src/avatars/thumbnail.py (no key-prefix guard), repo/docs/object-storage.md (object_created fires on every PUT, rule matches on key only)
defects.detect_if: says the notification rule filters on avatars/ which also matches the thumbnails written to avatars/thumb/, so every thumbnail write triggers the function again (infinite recursion/cost, and thumbnails of thumbnails), and that the trigger must be narrowed to avatars/orig/ or the output moved outside the prefix
defects.fixed_if: trigger prefix is avatars/orig/ (or outputs written under a prefix the rule does not match) and the doc states this

defects.title: Object key is derived from the user-supplied filename with no per-user component: users overwrite each other's avatars
defects.where: target.md 'Object layout' and the safe_name paragraph, 'Replacing and removing avatars'; repo/src/avatars/presign.py (key = KEY_PREFIX + safe_name(filename); confirm accepts any existing key under the prefix)
defects.detect_if: says two users who upload files with the same name (e.g. photo.jpg, me.png) write to the same key, so one overwrites the other's original and thumbnails (and a later replace/delete removes the other user's object); keys need a user id and/or random component. Also counts: the same user re-uploading a same-named file gets an unchanged key, so confirm deletes the just-uploaded object as the 'previous' one; or confirm accepts any existing key under avatars/orig/, so a user can adopt or later delete another user's object
defects.fixed_if: key includes the user id and a unique suffix (e.g. avatars/orig/<user_id>/<uuid>.<ext>) rather than just the filename

defects.title: 5 MB limit is not enforceable with a presigned PUT: the declared size is advisory
defects.where: target.md 'Upload flow' steps 1-2 (limit checked in client and against declared size); repo/docs/object-storage.md (body size is not part of the signature; use a POST policy with content-length-range); repo/src/avatars/presign.py (compares the client-declared size)
defects.detect_if: says the size check uses the client-declared size, so a caller can request a URL with a small declared size and PUT a much larger body (up to 5 GB per vendor doc); enforcing the limit needs a presigned POST policy with content-length-range (or a post-upload check that deletes oversize objects)
defects.fixed_if: design uses a POST policy with content-length-range (and constrained content type), or validates and deletes oversize objects after upload and says the PUT size is not enforced

defects.title: Product decision made silently: moderation model and retention of replaced avatars were decided by the authors without the T&S sign-off the policy requires
defects.where: target.md 'Replacing and removing avatars' (visible immediately, post-hoc reports only, previous objects deleted at once); repo/docs/policy/user-generated-content.md (requires a recorded T&S lead decision on moderation and on retention of replaced content)
defects.detect_if: points out that avatars are shown to other users with no review step and old avatars are hard-deleted on replacement, that these are moderation/retention choices the policy requires T&S to decide and sign off, and that this should be raised with the owner (T&S lead) as an open question rather than assumed
defects.fixed_if: the doc lists moderation model and retention of replaced/removed avatars as open decisions owned by T&S (or records the T&S decision and sign-off)

defects.title: Thumbnailer capacity is below launch peak: 6 executions / 1.2 s = 5 per second versus ~9 uploads per second, so a backlog builds and the UI's 10 s wait fails
defects.where: target.md 'Expected load' table and the paragraph after it (6 reserved executions, ~1.2 s each, ~9/s peak); repo/infra/storage.tf (reserved_concurrency = 6)
defects.detect_if: computes the capacity (6 / 1.2 s = about 5 thumbnails per second) against the stated ~9 uploads per second and concludes a backlog builds during the 10-minute peak (roughly 2,400 images behind, minutes of delay) so the 10 s UI poll gives up before thumbnails exist
defects.fixed_if: reserved concurrency is raised to cover the peak (about 11 or more at 1.2 s) or the expected delay is accepted and the UI handles late thumbnails; the arithmetic in the table is corrected

defects.title: A replaced avatar is not visible 'straight away': the key can be unchanged and the edge caches /avatars/* for 24 hours with no invalidation or versioned URL
defects.where: target.md 'Replacing and removing avatars' (user sees new image straight away) and 'Serving' (24 h cache); repo/infra/cdn.yaml (default_ttl_seconds and max_ttl_seconds 86400 on /avatars/*)
defects.detect_if: says that because avatar URLs are stable and cached for 24 hours at the edge (and in browsers), a user who replaces their avatar can keep seeing the old image until the cache expires unless URLs are versioned or the cache is invalidated
defects.fixed_if: new avatars get a new unique key/URL (or a version query parameter) or the doc specifies cache invalidation on confirm

traps.title: 60-second presigned URL expiry looks too short
traps.why_correct: target.md 'Upload flow' explains the URL is requested at Save time and used immediately, beta p99 transfer for 5 MB is 12 s, and docs/object-storage.md says expiry is evaluated when the request starts and in-flight transfers finish; presign.py passes URL_TTL_SECONDS = 60 to an expires_in argument in seconds. Flagging the TTL as too short is a false positive.

traps.title: No de-duplication for at-least-once notifications / retries in the thumbnailer
traps.why_correct: docs/object-storage.md says delivery is at least once, and the doc does not mention it, but thumbnail.py writes to deterministic keys derived from the object name, so running twice just overwrites identical output. Demanding an idempotency table is a false positive (the recursion in D2 is a separate problem).
